ドラッグで回転、ホイールまたはピンチで拡大。天体を選ぶと関連するアスペクトが強調: Drag to rotate; scroll or pinch to zoom. Select a body to highlight its aspects. With the canvas focused, use arrow keys to rotate and + / - to zoom.
3Dは観測地の地平線を水平面、天頂を上にした天球です。「地平線を水平に」で横から: The 3D sphere uses the observer's horizon as its horizontal plane, with the zenith above. Level horizon restores a side view. Ground view places you inside the sphere. Show below horizon is on by default, making the ground transparent; turn it off to hide bodies below the horizon. Ground view includes topocentric parallax at sea level, without atmospheric refraction or terrain. The table and aspects use geocentric values. In 2D, ecliptic latitude is flattened to zero and the ASC is on the left. Marker sizes and shading are illustrative, not actual lunar phases or surface features. Planets are spheres and sensitive points are faceted diamonds. The 22 background stars use Hipparcos positions, with proper motion, precession and nutation. Annual aberration, annual parallax and refraction are omitted.
ライト・ダーク・現地の空を切り替えられます。「現地の空」は選択中の地点・日時での: Choose Light, Dark or Local sky. Local sky approximates a clear daytime, twilight or night sky from the Sun's altitude at the selected place and time. In ground view, the sky follows the horizon and the Sun's bearing; background stars disappear in daylight. Body markers and aspects remain visible for reading the chart. Weather, moonlight, light pollution and atmospheric conditions are not modeled, and brightness is not a physical measurement. 2D uses a readable light or dark chart. Your theme also applies in Live sky mode.
1800〜2200年。「出生データを入力」で都市を選ぶと、当時の夏時間を含む時差: Supported dates: 1800-2200. Enter birth data lets you choose a city and calculates its historical UTC offset, including daylight saving time, in your browser. The direct inputs below use a fixed UTC offset. A calculated offset is fixed when the form is applied and stays fixed during playback. Location determines the horizon, ASC and MC. Supported latitude: -89 to +89 degrees.
日時・地点は端末内で計算し、アプリのサーバーへ送信しません。登録、広告、アクセス: Date, time and location are calculated on your device and are not sent to the app server. No registration, advertising, analytics or externally served fonts. Location is requested once, only after you press the button and grant browser permission. GPS, Wi-Fi or other methods depend on your device. Coordinates are not sent to the app server and are stored in this browser only if date and location saving is enabled. Your device and browser provider's terms apply to their location services. Selecting an additional body first loads about 3.5 MB of fixed astronomy data from this site, without input values. Saving is off by default. Date/location saving and display preference saving are separate. Only enabled categories are saved in this browser's localStorage. Display preferences include theme, playback speed, direction and range, house system and lines, aspect/point/body visibility, individual orbs and Lilith type. Turning saving off deletes that category. Leave saving off on shared devices. The hosting provider receives normal connection information.
「今の星を眺める」は現在時刻に1秒ごとに同期します。視点だけが約4分で1周し、回: Live sky synchronizes with the current time every second. The camera circles once in about four minutes; rotation can be paused. Back or Escape restores your original date and view. It uses the selected location and never starts GPS automatically.

表示中のヘッド・テイル・バーテックス・選択中のリリスを通常・複合アスペクトの判定: Visible nodes, Vertex and the selected Lilith are included in ordinary aspects and patterns. Turning this off keeps the points visible. The North-South Node pair is always excluded.
ヘッド／テイルは月の真交点（接触軌道）。月軌道と黄道の交点です。バーテックスは黄: The nodes are the Moon's true nodes from its osculating orbit, where the lunar orbital plane meets the ecliptic. Vertex is the western intersection of the ecliptic and prime vertical.
True Lilithは月の接触軌道の遠地点を近似計算します。平均リリスは月の平: True Lilith approximates the apogee of the Moon's osculating orbit. Mean Lilith uses the apogee of its mean orbit. Neither is asteroid Lilith. Both include ecliptic latitude in 3D. Against 199 Swiss Ephemeris samples, the maximum longitude difference was about 0.16 degrees for True and 0.0007 degrees for Mean. These are sample results, not error bounds for all dates.
移動軌跡は黄経の変化を示します。ヘッド／テイルは前後360日、バーテックスは前後: Trails show changes in ecliptic longitude: 360 days before and after for the nodes, and 12 hours before and after for Vertex. Thin surrounding lines are also visible in 2D.

ハウス分割は選択中の方式に連動します。キャンパナスは大円、プラシーダスは時間分割: House divisions follow the selected system. Campanus uses great circles; Placidus uses semi-arc curves. Equal and Whole Sign extend longitude sectors to the ecliptic poles. Placidus circumpolar regions are left undrawn.
地球中心・トロピカル黄道。Astronomy Engineで太陽から冥王星までを: Geocentric, tropical ecliptic. Astronomy Engine calculates the Sun through Pluto, targeting about one arcminute of accuracy. Eight additional bodies use interpolated geocentric, aberration-corrected NASA/JPL Horizons data transformed to the ecliptic of date. Interpolation errors were below one arcsecond at verification samples, not a guarantee for all dates. Aspects use ecliptic longitude differences, distinct from angular distance on the celestial sphere. Houses support Placidus, Campanus, Equal from ASC and Whole Sign. Placidus trisects each ecliptic point's diurnal and nocturnal arcs; Campanus divides the prime vertical to find ecliptic cusps. 3D house lines mark the ecliptic cusps. House divisions in Display settings also draws each system’s boundaries on the sphere. Where Placidus cannot be calculated near the poles, an explanation is shown and house lines are hidden; no automatic substitution occurs. 2D house lines and numbers 1-12 are on by default and can be toggled with House lines.

Equal and Whole Sign extend longitude sectors to the ecliptic poles. Placidus circumpolar regions are left undrawn. Stars in circumpolar regions never rise or never set at this latitude, so the line endings fade to mark where the divisions stop.

Equal, Whole Sign and Porphyry extend ecliptic longitude sectors to the ecliptic poles. Placidus omits circumpolar regions, where stars do not rise or set, and fades the line ends.
